checks.label: The mass behaves the same as an inductor, and the spring the same as an inverse capacitance: a loop with L = m, R = c and C = 1 ÷ k, stepped on its own in volts, traces the mass's height at 2.5, 5 and 10 s, for the opening values, every corner of the sliders and the 0.8 A start

At every moment the three terms add to zero: with the speed and acceleration read off each curve by small differences, m x″ + c x′ + k x stays within 0.0001 of 0 from 0.1 to 9.9 s, for both releases, the 0.8 A start and every corner of the sliders

Every number is right: −2, 0 and 2 N at the release, so x″ = −2 m/s²; 1.15, −0.37 and −0.78 N at 0.5 s, with 0.78 and −1.52 N for the slips; 2 V on 0.5 C at 0.25 F; a still moment within 0.01 s of 4.75 s, with store −0.61, loss 0 and inertia 0.61 N; 1 ÷ 0.5 = 2 and 1 ÷ 8 = 0.125; every setting swings; every trace stays inside ±0.6 and every bar inside ±2

The mass moves only up and down, level with its trace's newest point; on the side-by-side screen the capacitor's charge always equals the mass's height; and the bars added tip to tail end at 0 at every moment
Each puzzle accepts only its answer, draws it when it is checked, and draws every wrong pick as a mistake
Before Check, no puzzle's picture shows its answer or a mistake: the hidden bars read ?, and the matching springs are blank
Every demonstration has finished arriving within its 3 to 5 s, none starting before the 0.35 s screen fade ends; every answer's motion, right or wrong, finishes within 2 s
